records.title: Synthetic Student Paradox: reported spring 2026 course incident
records.ai_role: AI attributed by speaker; technical mechanism unverified
records.summary: Participant supplied classroom account attributed to Mansour Javidan reports roughly 140 enrollments, a little over 30 described as fraudulent, real identities used without consent, AI registration and subsequent student loan applications. Approval, disbursement and loss are unknown.

records.title: California Community Colleges fraud mechanisms
records.ai_role: Institution describes scripts and AI assisted simulated attendance
records.summary: Institutional description of stolen identity enrollment, bots, recruited straw students, simulated class attendance and financial aid fraud. Human and automated mechanisms can coexist.

records.title: California enrollment fraud controls and feedback
records.ai_role: Bot detection and machine learning feedback described
records.summary: August 2021 memorandum describes automated registration bot detection, machine learning application filtering, review deadlines and false positives affecting legitimate student accounts. Administrative labels require independent review before use as fraud ground truth.

records.title: Federal Student Aid identity confirmation and resolution
records.ai_role: AI involvement in specific incidents not established
records.summary: Federal guidance describes identity confirmation, review of fraud risk flags, administrator overrides and resolution options for admitted or enrolled students. Successful identity confirmation allows aid processing to continue.

records.title: Texas student aid identity fraud sentencing
records.summary: DOJ reports a guilty plea and sentencing involving false student identities and more than 100 aid applications. It reports over $1.3 million sought and $921,189.08 disbursed. This supplies a documented comparison for identity misuse; the release does not establish AI involvement.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case

records.title: Online college identity theft and aid refunds guilty plea
records.summary: DOJ reports an admitted scheme using stolen identities for online admission and aid, followed by withdrawal and refunds to controlled accounts. The release distinguishes $466,430 awarded from $211,820 disbursed. AI use is not established.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case

records.title: UK parliamentary findings on franchised student finance oversight
records.summary: The Public Accounts Committee reports fragmented oversight and detected fraud involving franchised higher education providers. This is a comparison about institutional incentives and accountability, not evidence of the same mechanism as the ASU account or of AI use.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case

records.title: Australian audit of education regulator fraud controls
records.summary: ANAO found partly effective fraud control arrangements at ASQA, including gaps in the regulatory risk environment and systematic control testing. This is a governance comparison, not an AI enrollment fraud finding.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case

records.title: Australian government account of ghost colleges
records.summary: The Commonwealth Fraud Prevention Centre describes providers enrolling students on paper without adequate education and subsequent regulatory action. The account supports comparison of enrollment incentives and education delivery. It does not establish bots or AI involvement.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case

records.title: Treasury referral of suspicious student aid transactions
records.summary: Treasury reports approximately $270 million in suspicious activity potentially linked to student aid fraud, referred as investigative leads. This amount is not an adjudicated fraud loss. The publication describes ghost and straw student schemes; specific AI attribution remains a separate evidence question.
records.ai_role: AI involvement not established for the specific case
